documents.title: Start with your own document
documents.description: Create a document with a title and category, or import an existing .hightex file. Click a document title to open it. You can write locally without signing in.

organize.title: Find the right document quickly
organize.description: Search by title or keywords, filter by category and choose an order. Use Select documents for bulk actions; Select visible applies only to the current results.

references.title: Keep references in one place
references.description: Add BibTeX or import from a local Zotero library in References. Your library stays available when you write; local writing does not require a cloud account.

chapters.title: Move between chapters without losing your place
chapters.description: Use the previous and next arrows to move through chapters in document order. The active chapter name appears in the middle. The next step shows how to pick a chapter directly.

exports.title: Details and exports are in the action menu
exports.description: Open the three-dot menu beside a document to edit its details or export to PDF or .hightex. In Indonesian titles and keywords, wrap a foreign term in underscores to display it in italics.

formatting.title: Format your text here
formatting.description: Select text to apply formatting, add headings, tables, figures or equations. The Save button stores your .hightex file.

chapterTree.title: Open your chapter sidebar
chapterTree.description: This button opens or closes the side panel. Open it to see Chapters, Preview, References, Settings and Variables. The following steps explain several tabs.

guide.waiting: Waiting for the control to appear…
guide.empty_organize: Create or import a document first. Its search, category and sorting controls will appear here. You can try this button now or continue the tour.
guide.empty_exports: Create or import a document first. Its three-dot menu will let you edit details or export PDF and .hightex.
guide.frozen_chapter: This section has its own form instead of a formatting toolbar. Use the chapter arrows to return to a normal chapter for text formatting.
guide.announcement_description: Explore these features with a short tour. Skipping marks every new guide in this list as seen.
guide.library_description: Choose a feature to learn about. You can replay its guide at any time.

documents.name: Create and open documents
documents.summary: Start a local document or import an existing .hightex file.

organize.name: Find and select documents
organize.summary: Search titles, filter categories, sort documents and select several at once.

references.name: Manage references
references.summary: Keep BibTeX and import your Zotero library for use while writing.

exports.name: Document details and exports
exports.summary: Edit document details and export PDF or .hightex from the action menu.

chapters.name: Navigate chapters
chapters.summary: Use chapter arrows, Mod+number from the schema, or Mod+0 for the appendix.

formatting.name: Format your writing
formatting.summary: Explore the toolbar for headings, text formatting, tables, figures and equations.

chapterTree.name: Chapter and reference sidebar
chapterTree.summary: Open chapters, preview, references and document settings from the sidebar.

writing.name: Start writing and structure chapters
writing.summary: Learn paragraphs, H2/H3 for hierarchy and H4 for paragraphs without indentation.

paragraphs.title: Start with body paragraphs
paragraphs.description: Click a paragraph below the chapter title to write. Enter starts a new paragraph; Shift+Enter adds a line within the same paragraph. Avoid repeated spaces for alignment; the document format controls the page layout.

headings.title: Structure the outline with H2 and H3
headings.description: HighTex prepares the chapter title (H1). Choose H2 for sections and H3 for subsections; enter their titles without numbers because numbering is automatic. H4 is a paragraph style without indentation, outside the hierarchy; it does not appear in the outline or table of contents.
headings.example:
H2: Research Methods
H3: Data Collection
H4: A paragraph without indentation, outside the hierarchy

formatting.name: Text formatting and lists
formatting.summary: Use italics, bold and lists without manually managing numbering.

emphasis.title: Format selected words or sentences
emphasis.description: Select text, then use I for italics or B for bold. Use italics for foreign terms in the body. Command/Ctrl+I and Command/Ctrl+B are also available. The underscore convention for titles and keywords is explained in the document details guide.

lists.title: Use the toolbar for lists
lists.description: Choose a bulleted or numbered list for details. Enter adds an item; Enter on an empty item ends the list. Use numbered lists for ordered steps so numbering follows content changes.

details.name: Titles, author details and keywords
details.summary: Set document details and abstract keywords in both languages.

metadata.title: Complete the document details
metadata.description: Document settings contain Indonesian and English titles, category and author details. Wrap foreign terms in an Indonesian title with underscores to display italics. Use the panel Save button after editing. Academic details supplied by the cloud may be locked to the server data.

keywords.title: Add keywords to the abstract
keywords.description: At the end of the Indonesian abstract, enter a keyword then press Enter or comma. Each language supports up to five keywords; use × to remove one. Wrap foreign terms in Indonesian keywords with underscores. Enter English keywords in the Abstract section; they display as written.

figures.name: Figures and tables
figures.summary: Insert figures, numbered tables and layout grids for the right purpose.

figures.title: Insert a figure and its caption
figures.description: Place the cursor where the figure belongs, then use the image button to insert a Figure Image. Choose an image file and enter its caption; figure numbering is automatic. You can also type this shortcut and choose its suggestion.

tables.title: Use a captioned table for data
tables.description: This table button inserts a Figure Table with a header, caption and automatic number. Fill in column names and data, then update the caption. The shortcut takes columns, rows and caption in that order; underscores in its caption become spaces.

grid.title: Distinguish data tables from layout grids
grid.description: The grid button inserts a table for arranging content. A layout grid has no caption or table number like a Figure Table. Use Figure Table for data you intend to reference as a numbered table in your writing.

equations.name: Formulas and equations
equations.summary: Write LaTeX as a displayed equation or a formula within a sentence.

block_math.title: Create an equation with LaTeX
block_math.description: Use Σ to insert an equation and enter its LaTeX. You can also type the example below as its own paragraph. Reference an equation with /eq so its number in the text follows the equation.

inline_math.title: Short formulas within a sentence
inline_math.description: For a formula within a sentence, wrap its LaTeX in a single dollar sign on each side. Use a displayed equation when it needs a number and a reference.

citations.name: Citations and bibliography
citations.summary: Add sources, insert citations and understand the automatic bibliography.

citation_library.title: Prepare sources in your reference library
citation_library.description: Add BibTeX or import Zotero sources in this panel. Search for a source; Copy copies a citation you can paste into the text. A source stored only in the library does not yet belong to the document bibliography.

cite_in_text.title: Insert HighTex citations in your text
cite_in_text.description: Place the cursor after a sourced statement, type @ or #, and choose its reference. You can also paste a citation copied from the library. Author names and years entered as ordinary text are not recognized as HighTex citations.

bibliography.title: The bibliography follows citations you use
bibliography.description: HighTex builds the bibliography from citations actually used in the document. If it is empty, check that your citations point to valid sources. Open the preview to inspect the result; you do not need to type a bibliography manually into a chapter.

referencesAliases.name: Object references and aliases
referencesAliases.summary: Reference figure, table and equation numbers, and define abbreviations.

object_references.title: Reference objects instead of typing their numbers
object_references.description: Type /img, /table or /eq and choose the object you want to mention. Alternatively, open the object settings, choose Copy Ref and paste it into a sentence. References follow object numbering when the order changes; plain text such as Gambar 1.2 does not.

aliases.title: Define an abbreviation with an alias
aliases.description: Select a single abbreviation, such as API. In the selection menu, choose alias creation, enter its expansion and save it. Aliases belong to this document and sort automatically. Ordinary text without an alias has no associated definition.

variables.name: Variables and symbols
variables.summary: Store reusable values and insert variables or symbols through suggestions.

manage_variables.title: Store values you use repeatedly
manage_variables.description: Add a variable as name=value. Use a short name without spaces. Built-in variables such as title, altTitle and chapter1 follow document data and cannot be replaced with custom variables.

insert_variables.title: Choose a variable from suggestions
insert_variables.description: In the body, type a backslash followed by a variable name and choose its suggestion. Variables keep repeated values consistent. Symbols such as alpha are also available through backslash suggestions.

reviewSave.name: Find, save and export
reviewSave.summary: Review your text, save an editable file and produce a final PDF.

find.title: Find text before replacing it
find.description: Use Search or Command/Ctrl+F to find text in the active chapter. Review matches before replacing one or all occurrences, especially when a term appears in different contexts.

save.title: Save a .hightex file for future editing
save.description: Your writing is stored locally as you type. Save or Command/Ctrl+S writes a .hightex file to your chosen location; watch the button status. Keep this file to continue editing or move your work.

preview.title: Check the page layout in the preview
preview.description: Open the preview tab to inspect layout, heading numbers, figures, tables, references and bibliography. The final pages follow the document category format.

pdf.title: Export PDF after reviewing the result
pdf.description: Use Export PDF to create a file ready to read or share. Wait for the process to finish and choose a save location if prompted. Keep the .hightex file so the document remains editable.

forms.name: Generate a form package
forms.summary: Prepare proposal or defense forms from your document, check the preview, and download separate PDFs in a ZIP.
forms.empty: There are no documents yet. Create or import a .hightex file on Documents, then reopen this guide.

document.title: Start with the document you need
document.description: Choose the document to prepare forms for. Its title and author details follow your selection.

stage.title: Choose proposal or defense
stage.description: Choose proposal or defense. B0/B1 are proposal-only; B3 is available for both stages.

selection.title: Select the forms to download
selection.description: Check the forms to include in the ZIP. Click a title to preview it without changing its checkbox.

data.title: Fill in only the missing details
data.description: Expand administration details to fill in additional fields. Author and lecturer details follow the document profile; edit that profile in the editor if needed.

preview.title: Check the result before printing
preview.description: Check names, staff numbers, and page layout. Grades, comments, corrections, and signatures stay blank for faculty to complete.

export.title: Download separate PDFs in one ZIP
export.description: Download ZIP creates separate PDFs for the selected forms. Fill in the author name/student number and select at least one form to enable it.

forms.select_first: Choose a document to continue. If you have no documents, close this guide and create or import one first.

lecturers.name: Choose lecturers and save a default profile
lecturers.summary: Search by name or staff number, choose advisors and examiners, and save your selections for offline use.

advisors.title: Choose advisors from the directory
advisors.description: Search for an advisor by name or staff number; their number follows your selection. Add a second advisor if needed.

refresh.title: Keep using the directory offline
refresh.description: Your saved directory works offline. Refresh directory when online, then select a lecturer again to use updated names or staff numbers.

committee.title: Choose the chair and examiners
committee.description: Expand this section to choose the chair and both examiners. Their names and staff numbers are saved with the profile.

save.title: Save defaults for later use
save.description: Save your defaults for later use. Existing documents keep their own profiles; use local defaults in the editor to review and apply changes.

identity.title: Enter your default author details
identity.description: Enter your name and student number to reuse in documents. This profile is stored locally on your device.

documentProfile.name: Author and lecturer details per document
documentProfile.summary: Set the author, advisors, chair, and examiners for this document independently of other documents.

profile.title: Each document keeps its own profile
profile.description: Author and lecturer details here supply this document and its forms. Internship advisors remain manual.

defaults.title: Copy defaults when you need them
defaults.description: Use local defaults lets you review and select changes before applying them. Empty defaults never clear existing details automatically.

documentProfile.locked: This document uses cloud academic data for author details and lecturer assignments. Use local defaults is unavailable while those fields are locked. Update them through the server data source.

save.title: Save the document profile changes
save.description: Profile changes first enter the settings draft. Use Save to apply them to this document.

create.title: Create a document from a category
create.description: Choose Create document, select a category and enter a title. The category determines the chapter structure. Your local profile is copied into the new document and can be edited separately.

import.title: Import an existing archive
import.description: Use Import to select a .hightex file containing chapters, the document profile, references and assets. If its document ID already exists, the import dialog lets you choose how to handle the conflict.

open.title: Continue writing
open.description: Click a document title to open its editor window. Local documents can be edited offline. This tour points out the controls; you choose whether to open the editor.
open.empty: No documents are visible yet. Create or import a document, then click its title to open the editor.

search.title: Search titles and keywords
search.description: Type part of a title or keyword to narrow the list. Clear the search to show documents again. Searching does not change document content.

category.title: Filter by category
category.description: Select a category to show its documents. Choose All categories to show every category again. This filter does not change any document category.

sort.title: Sort the list
sort.description: Sort by update time or title. Combine sorting with search and the category filter to find the document you want to continue.

select.title: Select multiple documents
select.description: Enter selection mode and check the documents to process together. Check the selection count before exporting or deleting. Leave selection mode to open documents by their titles again.

bibtex.title: Add BibTeX references
bibtex.description: Open Add, then paste BibTeX or select a file. Each reference has a citation key, such as methods2026, which you use when inserting citations in the editor.

zotero.title: Import from local Zotero
zotero.description: Run Zotero and enable its local HTTP access. Enable the Zotero integration in Settings, then use this button to select references. The tour does not start an import automatically.

search.title: Find a reference
search.description: Search the information shown in the list, such as citation keys, titles or authors. Clear the search if a newly imported reference is missing from view.

library.title: Review and use references
library.description: Check each reference key and title. The copy button copies its reference text. To cite it in your writing, open the editor References panel and select its citation key.
library.empty: No references are visible. Clear the search, add BibTeX or import from Zotero, then review the results here.

actions.title: Choose the output you need
actions.description: Open the document menu for details and export options. PDF is for reading or printing; .hightex preserves an editable document that can be imported again. The tour does not export automatically.

many.title: Export multiple documents
many.description: Enter selection mode and check documents to use the bulk export actions. Review your selection before running an action. A single document can also be exported from its menu.

location.title: Choose the export location
location.description: Choose whether to ask for a file location each time or use the default export folder. These settings control exports; saving in the editor uses the archive location for the open document.

jump.title: Jump through the chapter list
jump.description: Select a chapter title to jump directly to it. Expand a chapter to see its headings and jump to a section. Number shortcuts also work while the panel is closed.
jump.example:
Mod + 1 … 9 → main chapter
Mod = ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl on Windows/Linux

appendix.title: Open the appendices
appendix.description: Appendices have their own section after the main chapters. Open it from the list, then use headings to separate individual appendices.
appendix.example:
Mod + 0 → appendices
Mod + N → next chapter

chapters.title: Chapters and headings
chapters.description: The Chapters panel lists the document structure and written headings. Click an item to navigate. Opening or closing the panel does not change your writing.

citations.title: References while writing
citations.description: Use the References tab to find citation keys to insert. This panel sits beside your writing; the full reference library is also available in the workspace.

settings.title: Details for this document
settings.description: The Settings tab contains details and the profile of the open document. Review changes and save them from this panel. Changing your local profile does not automatically replace profiles in existing documents.

walkthrough.requires_document: This step needs a document. Close the tour, create or import a document, then reopen the guide from Help.
walkthrough.requires_visible_document: Show at least one document to continue. Clear the filters, or close the tour and create or import a document first.
